posts.body_html:
I'm not completely sure what the story is behind this plant, but it originally came from Jerry Addington. I believe he crossed a bunch of different S. roseas and even venosas together, and out of one of the crosses came this gigantic thing. If you've ever seen giant roseas, they look unreal...I don't think they get this big in the wild, but you never know.

Anyways, below is a photo of S. purp. 'big mama' grown by Rob Co of the Pitcher plant Project. Pitchers haven't formed yet, but this plant is in full bloom. Flowers are a bit bigger than your "normal" S. rosea, and they smell really sweet. I have a piece of this clone in my collection, so this will be an ongoing thread:

posts.body_html:
salpinx-not positive what your question is, but here's some more details to clarify things. Jerry has made a ton of purpurea crosses-he didn't keep track if it was Rosea x venosa, or Rosea x Rosea, etc. In the end, out of the many different seed batches, some individuals turned out to be gigantic, and this is where Rob's oriignal "big mama" comes from.

I think the real question is do we call any gigantic "rosea dominant" plant "big mama" or is it just one clone? If we just label one clone big mama, what do we call the rest of them? It's a pretty messy situation in my opinion, and I don't have an answer on that one. In any case, all of these various rosea hybrid clones can produce obscenely gigantic pitchers. Keep in mind that there are some pure S. rosea from Liberty Co, FL, for example, that can also get gigantic.

posts.body_html:
Howdy! Actually... I got S. "Big Mama" from Phil Faulisi and Don Elkins. It's a different plant and not the one in the center photograph. A portion of the "Big Mama" is in the lower left of the photo in the circular pot. I don't know the exact background of S. "Big Mama" but when I hear back from Don I'll let you know.

The plant flowering in the photo is from Jerry Addington, which he originally received from some old school nursery way back in the day - either Lee's Botanical or Orgels he tells me. Those are ones he did *not* breed, but rather he received them with that label from the original source. I've kept that tag/label too, but will revise my records accordingly. I know of Meadowview's "Caroline" that you mention, but the one photographed above is a different plant. Hope that helps, Salpinx!

Jerry has done a lot of crosses with different purps as Mike mentioned, but the one in flower in the photo isn't it. An example of one of those purps is also in the photo. It would be the plant behind the flowering plant - the really ruffled one. I got that from Jerry too.

Hope this clarifies things!
